title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 8
statement: Emmy says to Max, “I ordered \(36\) math club sweatshirts today.” Max asks, “How much did each shirt cost?” Emmy responds, “I’ll give you a hint. The total cost was \(\$\underline{A}\,\underline{B}\,\underline{B}.\underline{B}\,\underline{A},\) where \(A\) and \(B\) are digits and \(A \ne 0.\)” After a pause, Max says, “That was a good price.” What is \(A + B?\)

solutions.text: In cents the total is \(10000A + 1000B + 100B\) \(+ 10B + A\) \(= 10001A + 1110B.\) Split evenly among \(36\) shirts, so it’s divisible by \(36.\) Now \(10001 \equiv 29\) and \(1110 \equiv 30 \pmod{36},\) so we need \(29A + 30B \equiv 0,\) which reduces to \(7A + 6B \equiv 0 \pmod{36}.\) The only digit solution with \(A \ne 0\) is \(A = 6, B = 5,\) since \(7 \cdot 6 + 6 \cdot 5 = 72.\) That’s \(\$655.56,\) or \(\$18.21\) a shirt, so \(A + B = 11.\) Therefore, the answer is C.
hints: Write the total in cents: \(\underline{A}\,\underline{B}\,\underline{B}.\underline{B}\,\underline{A}\) is \(10001A + 1110B\) cents, and it must be divisible by \(36\)
Reduce the condition modulo \(36\) to \(7A + 6B \equiv 0;\) test digits to find the unique \(A, B\)
